architecture.rationale: A deterministic self-evolution decision kernel now separates proposals, signals and promotion decisions; automated branch generation remains future work.

autonomy.rationale: Louis OS can evaluate bounded self-improvement candidates autonomously, but it does not yet author and submit every candidate end to end.

initiative.rationale: The evolution policy defines a detect-to-learn loop, while production bottleneck detection still needs workflow integration.

results.rationale: Self-evolution is aligned to verified autonomous revenue while protecting guarded metrics; no revenue gain from an evolved candidate is yet evidenced.

robustness.rationale: Promotion is blocked on failed tests, failed deterministic checks, absent evidence or any guarded regression.

safety.rationale: Non-reversible candidates and high-risk autonomous promotions are held by default.

memory.rationale: The policy requires lessons to be recorded, while persistence of evolution histories is not yet wired to Firestore.

validations.capability: Louis OS can deterministically promote, hold or roll back a candidate based on reversibility, risk, tests, deterministic checks and guarded metric deltas.
